title: Analgesia, sedation and delirium
summary: Analgesia, sedation and delirium in the ICU (PADIS 2018 and 2025 update, eCASH): pain assessment and analgosedation, RASS-guided light sedation and agent choice, CAM-ICU delirium care, neuromuscular blockade, and alcohol withdrawal.

topics.title: Pain assessment and analgesia-first sedation (PADIS, eCASH)
topics.summary: Assess pain with NRS, CPOT or BPS, treat pain first with multimodal opioid-sparing analgesia, and aim for calm, comfortable, collaborative patients.

definition.text: PADIS/eCASH: early Comfort using Analgesia, minimal Sedatives and maximal Humane care - pain first, light sedation, and the ABCDEF bundle (Assess pain, Both SAT and SBT, Choice of sedation, Delirium, Early mobility, Family).

steps.title: Assess pain routinely
steps.detail: Self-report (NRS 0-10) when possible; CPOT (0-8, > 2 = pain) or BPS (3-12, > 5 = pain) when the patient cannot communicate; assess at least every 4 h and before procedures.

steps.title: Analgesia first
steps.detail: Treat pain before giving sedatives (analgosedation): fentanyl boluses/infusion titrated to CPOT/BPS.

steps.title: Multimodal, opioid-sparing
steps.detail: Regular paracetamol; low-dose ketamine in surgical patients; neuropathic agents (gabapentin/pregabalin); regional blocks (epidural, erector spinae, serratus) for chest/abdominal trauma or surgery.

steps.title: Procedural analgesia
steps.detail: Pre-emptive fentanyl bolus or local anaesthetic before chest drain removal, line insertion, turning and wound care.

steps.title: Humane care
steps.detail: Explain, reorient, sleep promotion, hearing aids/glasses, family presence, music; treat thirst and anxiety.

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: start 50 mcg/h = 5 mL/h; bolus 25-50 mcg for CPOT > 2

doseCards.notes: 2-3 g/day in liver disease or < 50 kg.

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 0.1 mg/kg/h = 7 mg/h (0.7 mL/h of 10 mg/mL)

tables.title: Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT)
rows: Protection (slow, cautious movements, touching pain site)
tables.caption: Score 0-8; > 2 indicates significant pain.

redFlags.text: Agitation in a ventilated patient: first exclude pain, hypoxia, hypercapnia, tube displacement, full bladder, and withdrawal before deepening sedation.

pitfalls.text: Using vital signs alone to judge pain: they are unreliable.

pearls.text: A comfortable, awake, interactive patient on a ventilator is the goal, not an immobile one.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Pain in ICU arises from surgery, trauma, tubes, suction, turning and immobility, and drives stress responses, sleep loss, delirium and chronic pain after ICU.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- PADIS 2018 guidelines [Devlin 2018]; 2025 focused update [Lewis 2025]; eCASH concept [Vincent 2016].
- CPOT validation [Gelinas 2006].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Opioid-heavy analgosedation and opioid tolerance/hyperalgesia; long-term opioid use after ICU.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Fentanyl, morphine, ketamine and IV paracetamol are widely available in India; regional analgesia for rib fractures is underused.
- Nursing ratios (often 1:2 or worse) make protocolised, nurse-driven pain and sedation assessment especially valuable.

topics.title: Sedation targets, RASS and sedative choice
topics.summary: Target light sedation (RASS -1 to 0) with daily awakening, prefer propofol or dexmedetomidine over benzodiazepines, and reserve deep sedation for specific indications.

definition.text: RASS ranges from +4 (combative) to -5 (unrousable). Light sedation (RASS -2 to 0) is the default; deep sedation (RASS -4 to -5) only for specific indications (severe ARDS with NMB, raised ICP, status epilepticus, TTM shivering).

steps.title: Set a target
steps.detail: Document a RASS target every shift (usually -1 to 0); assess RASS every 2-4 h.

steps.title: Choose agent
steps.detail: Propofol or dexmedetomidine rather than benzodiazepines; PADIS 2025 suggests dexmedetomidine over propofol for light sedation (less delirium, more time at target, more bradycardia).

steps.title: Daily SAT paired with SBT
steps.detail: Stop or reduce sedation daily (if no contraindication) and pair with a spontaneous breathing trial (ABC trial).

steps.title: Benzodiazepines only when needed
steps.detail: Alcohol/benzodiazepine withdrawal, seizures, deep sedation when propofol limited, palliative sedation.

steps.title: Deep sedation indications
steps.detail: Use with NMB, refractory ICP, status epilepticus; monitor with BIS/EEG where available; reassess daily.

steps.title: Weaning
steps.detail: Taper long infusions (> 5-7 days) to avoid iatrogenic withdrawal; consider enteral clonidine or dexmedetomidine to transition.

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg at 1.5 mg/kg/h = 105 mg/h = 10.5 mL/h (count 1.1 kcal/mL as fat calories)

tables.title: Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale
rows: Agitated, frequent non-purposeful movement, fights ventilator
Drowsy, sustained awakening to voice (eye contact > 10 s)
Light sedation, briefly awakens to voice (< 10 s)
Moderate sedation, movement or eye opening to voice, no eye contact
Deep sedation, no response to voice, movement to physical stimulation
Unrousable, no response to voice or physical stimulation

redFlags.text: Propofol > 4 mg/kg/h or long infusions with unexplained metabolic acidosis, rising CK, lipaemia or arrhythmia: propofol infusion syndrome - stop propofol.

pitfalls.text: Benzodiazepine infusions as routine sedation: more delirium and longer ventilation.
Early dexmedetomidine as sole sedative in older patients (SPICE III signal of increased mortality in > 65 years).

pearls.text: Agitation on waking during SAT often signals pain or delirium - treat the cause, then restart at half the previous dose if needed.

nodes.text: Exclude hypoxia, tube issues, bladder, withdrawal; screen delirium

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Deep sedation in the first 48 h is independently associated with longer ventilation, delirium and death. Benzodiazepines act on GABA-A receptors and are strongly deliriogenic; dexmedetomidine acts on central alpha-2 receptors producing rousable sedation with preserved respiratory drive.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ABC trial: paired SAT + SBT reduced mortality at 1 year [Girard 2008].
- SPICE III (4,000 patients): early dexmedetomidine did not reduce mortality; more bradycardia/hypotension; possible harm in older patients [Shehabi 2019].
- MENDS2: dexmedetomidine vs propofol in sepsis - no difference in delirium-free days [Hughes 2021].
- PADIS 2025: conditional recommendation for dexmedetomidine over propofol for light sedation [Lewis 2025].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Dexmedetomidine vs propofol (MENDS2 neutral vs PADIS 2025 conditional preference); inhaled sedation (volatile agents).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Generic dexmedetomidine and propofol are relatively affordable in India; midazolam infusions remain common due to cost and habit - an important quality-improvement target.
- Infusion pump availability may limit titration in smaller ICUs; intermittent boluses guided by RASS are a fallback.

topics.title: Delirium: CAM-ICU screening, prevention and management
topics.summary: Screen every shift with CAM-ICU, prevent with the ABCDEF bundle, treat causes, and use antipsychotics only for distressing agitation.

definition.text: Delirium: acute fluctuating disturbance of attention and awareness. CAM-ICU positive = feature 1 (acute change or fluctuation) + feature 2 (inattention) + either feature 3 (altered level of consciousness, RASS ≠ 0) or feature 4 (disorganised thinking). Subtypes: hypoactive (commonest, often missed), hyperactive, mixed.

steps.title: Screen every shift
steps.detail: CAM-ICU (or ICDSC) when RASS ≥ -3; document result.

steps.title: Look for causes (THINK)
steps.detail: Toxic (drugs: benzodiazepines, anticholinergics, steroids; withdrawal), Hypoxaemia, Infection/sepsis, Non-pharmacological factors (immobility, sleep deprivation, no glasses/hearing aids), K+/electrolytes/glucose/urea; also urinary retention, constipation, pain, alcohol withdrawal.

steps.title: Prevent - ABCDEF bundle
steps.detail: Minimise benzodiazepines, light sedation, SAT/SBT, early and enhanced mobilisation, sleep hygiene (lights, noise, melatonin), reorientation, family involvement.

steps.title: Hyperactive delirium endangering safety
steps.detail: Ensure analgesia; dexmedetomidine for agitation preventing extubation; short course of haloperidol 2.5-5 mg IV or quetiapine for distressing agitation; avoid physical restraints where possible.

steps.title: Do not routinely use antipsychotics
steps.detail: Neither haloperidol nor ziprasidone shortened delirium (MIND-USA); PADIS 2025 makes no recommendation for routine antipsychotic treatment.

steps.title: Follow-up
steps.detail: Delirium predicts long-term cognitive impairment: inform family, ICU follow-up clinic where available.

doseCards.dose: 2.5-5 mg every 6-8 h as needed (max ~20 mg/day)
doseCards.notes: Check QTc; lower doses in elderly.

tables.title: CAM-ICU
rows: Different from baseline, or fluctuating RASS/GCS in last 24 h
Squeeze hand on letter 'A' in SAVEAHAART: > 2 errors = positive
Yes/no questions (e.g. 'Will a stone float on water?') + command; > 1 error = positive
tables.caption: Delirium = 1 + 2 + (3 or 4). Not assessable if RASS -4/-5.

redFlags.text: New delirium may be the first sign of sepsis, hypoxia, hypoglycaemia, stroke or alcohol withdrawal.

pitfalls.text: Missing hypoactive delirium in a 'quiet, good' patient.
Using benzodiazepines for delirium (except alcohol/benzodiazepine withdrawal).

pearls.text: Family presence and familiar voices are among the most effective non-drug measures.

nodes.text: THINK: drugs, hypoxia, infection, environment, electrolytes; treat pain
Review daily; stop antipsychotic when resolved

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Delirium results from neuroinflammation, neurotransmitter imbalance (cholinergic deficiency, dopaminergic excess), impaired cerebral perfusion and oxygenation, sleep disruption and drug effects, superimposed on vulnerability (age, dementia, alcohol).
consultantNotes.evidence:
- CAM-ICU validation [Ely 2001].
- MIND-USA: haloperidol/ziprasidone did not shorten delirium [Girard 2018]. AID-ICU: haloperidol did not significantly increase days alive and out of hospital [Andersen-Ranberg 2022].
- PADIS 2025: enhanced mobilisation and melatonin suggested; no recommendation on antipsychotics [Lewis 2025].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Antipsychotics for hyperactive delirium; prophylactic dexmedetomidine at night.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Validated Hindi and other Indian language versions of CAM-ICU are used in some centres; translate the inattention test letters appropriately.
- Families are often present for long hours in Indian ICUs - use them for reorientation and comfort.

topics.title: Neuromuscular blockade in the ICU
topics.summary: Indications, deep sedation first, agent choice, train-of-four monitoring, and complications of sustained NMB.

definition.text: Sustained NMB abolishes patient effort and shivering. ICU indications: severe ARDS with dyssynchrony or high plateau pressure, refractory intracranial hypertension, shivering during targeted temperature management, status asthmaticus with dyssynchrony, abdominal compartment syndrome.

steps.title: Confirm indication
steps.detail: Use NMB selectively (ROSE: routine early NMB in moderate-severe ARDS did not reduce mortality); consider in PaO2/FiO2 < 150 with dyssynchrony or high pressures despite optimal settings.

steps.title: Deep sedation and analgesia first
steps.detail: Achieve RASS -5 and adequate analgesia before starting; awareness under paralysis is a serious harm; use BIS where available.

steps.title: Choose agent
steps.detail: Cisatracurium/atracurium (organ-independent Hofmann elimination) preferred in hepatic/renal failure; rocuronium/vecuronium alternatives.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.detail: Train-of-four target 1-2/4 twitches combined with clinical assessment (ventilator synchrony); daily interruption when possible.

steps.title: Prevent complications
steps.detail: Eye care (lubricant, taping), pressure area care, DVT prophylaxis, glucose control, minimise steroids; stop as soon as indication resolves (typically ≤ 48 h).

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg at 2 mcg/kg/min = 140 mcg/min = 8.4 mg/h = 4.2 mL/h

redFlags.text: Paralysed patient with tachycardia, hypertension, lacrimation: possible awareness - deepen sedation and analgesia immediately.

pitfalls.text: Forgetting eye care: corneal abrasions and exposure keratopathy.

pearls.text: Peripheral nerve stimulation can be misleading with oedema or hypothermia; combine with clinical end-points.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: NMB reduces oxygen consumption and patient-ventilator dyssynchrony, may lessen ventilator-induced lung injury (reducing transpulmonary pressure swings and pendelluft), and abolishes shivering; costs include ICU-acquired weakness and loss of neurological examination.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- SCCM 2016 NMB guidelines [Murray 2016].
- ROSE: early routine cisatracurium in moderate-severe ARDS - no mortality benefit (lighter sedation in control arm) [PETAL 2019].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Role of NMB in severe ARDS after ROSE; best monitoring method.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Atracurium and vecuronium are cheaper and widely available in India; cisatracurium availability and cost vary.
- Train-of-four monitors are not available in all ICUs; clinical end-points plus scheduled interruptions are used.

topics.title: Alcohol withdrawal and delirium tremens
topics.summary: Recognise withdrawal timelines, use CIWA-Ar and symptom-triggered or front-loaded benzodiazepines, add phenobarbital for resistance, give thiamine first and treat complications.

definition.text: Alcohol withdrawal: tremor, anxiety, sweating, tachycardia 6-24 h after the last drink; seizures 6-48 h; hallucinosis 12-48 h; delirium tremens (DTs) 48-96 h with confusion, autonomic instability and hyperthermia (mortality up to 5% treated).

steps.title: Assess
steps.detail: CIWA-Ar (if able to communicate; > 15 severe) or RASS/MINDS in ICU; history of DTs or withdrawal seizures predicts severe course; check glucose, electrolytes (Mg, PO4, K), LFT, CT head after fall/first seizure.

steps.title: Thiamine before glucose
steps.detail: Thiamine 200-500 mg IV three times daily for suspected Wernicke (confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia - any one in at-risk patient), otherwise 100-200 mg daily.

steps.title: Benzodiazepines
steps.detail: Symptom-triggered or front-loaded diazepam (10-20 mg every 1-2 h orally, or 5-10 mg IV every 5-10 min for severe), lorazepam in liver failure/elderly; target light sedation (RASS 0 to -1).

steps.title: Resistant withdrawal
steps.detail: High benzodiazepine requirements (e.g. diazepam > 50-100 mg/h): phenobarbital 10 mg/kg IV or incremental doses; propofol or dexmedetomidine as adjuncts in ventilated patients (dexmedetomidine does not prevent seizures).

steps.title: Supportive
steps.detail: Fluids, correct Mg/K/PO4 (refeeding risk), cooling for hyperthermia, nutrition; avoid antipsychotics as monotherapy (lower seizure threshold).

steps.title: After recovery
steps.detail: Brief intervention, de-addiction referral, consider naltrexone/acamprosate (if liver allows) or baclofen in cirrhosis.

doseCards.dose: 5-10 mg every 5-10 min until calm (light sedation)
doseCards.workedExample: Typical DTs: 10 mg IV, repeat every 10 min; total may exceed 100 mg in first hours
IBW 65 kg: 650 mg in 100 mL NS over 30 min; monitor airway

doseCards.dose: 200-500 mg three times daily for 3-5 days

redFlags.text: Fever, tachycardia > 120, agitation and confusion 2-4 days after admission in a drinker: delirium tremens - ICU care.

pitfalls.text: Giving dextrose before thiamine in malnourished drinkers (may precipitate Wernicke).
Missing concurrent sepsis, pancreatitis, head injury or hepatic encephalopathy.

pearls.text: Admission to ICU for an unrelated problem (trauma, surgery, pneumonia) is a common setting for unrecognised withdrawal - take an alcohol history from family.

nodes.text: Thiamine IV before glucose; electrolytes, Mg
IV diazepam/lorazepam boluses to light sedation

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Chronic alcohol enhances GABA-A and inhibits NMDA receptors; abrupt cessation produces GABA hypofunction and glutamate excess with sympathetic overactivity, seizures and delirium. Kindling makes each episode more severe.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Phenobarbital monotherapy vs benzodiazepines in ICU; high-dose thiamine dosing.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Alcohol use disorder is common in Indian men; country liquor and illicit liquor (methanol risk) may complicate presentations.
- Diazepam, lorazepam (oral more than IV), phenobarbital and thiamine are widely available; Pabrinex-type high-potency B-vitamin injections are not uniformly available.

drugs.name: Fentanyl
drugs.adultDose: Bolus 25-100 mcg IV; infusion 25-200 mcg/h (about 0.5-3 mcg/kg/h), titrated to CPOT/BPS.
drugs.preparationIndia: 50 mcg/mL; e.g. 500 mcg in 50 mL = 10 mcg/mL.
drugs.cautions: Accumulates with prolonged infusion (context-sensitive half-life), chest wall rigidity with large boluses, constipation.

drugs.name: Paracetamol
drugs.adultDose: 1 g IV/oral every 6 h (max 4 g/day; 2-3 g/day if weight < 50 kg, malnutrition, chronic alcohol use or liver disease).

drugs.name: Ketamine
drugs.indications: Adjunct analgesia (opioid-sparing), sedation in bronchospasm/haemodynamic instability
drugs.adultDose: Analgesia: 0.1-0.5 mg/kg IV bolus, then 0.05-0.4 mg/kg/h. Sedation: 0.5-2 mg/kg/h.

drugs.name: Morphine
drugs.renalHepatic: Active metabolite (M6G) accumulates in AKI - prefer fentanyl.

drugs.name: Propofol
drugs.adultDose: 0.3-3 mg/kg/h (5-50 mcg/kg/min) infusion; avoid > 4 mg/kg/h for > 48 h.
drugs.cautions: Hypotension, hypertriglyceridaemia (lipid 1.1 kcal/mL), propofol infusion syndrome (acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, arrhythmia).
drugs.monitoring: Triglycerides every 48-72 h; CK/lactate if high dose.

drugs.name: Dexmedetomidine
drugs.adultDose: 0.2-1.4 mcg/kg/h infusion (loading dose usually omitted in ICU because of bradycardia/hypotension).
drugs.preparationIndia: 100 mcg/mL; 200 mcg in 50 mL NS = 4 mcg/mL.
drugs.cautions: Bradycardia, hypotension; does not provide deep sedation alone; SPICE III signal of harm in older patients (> 65) when used as early sole sedative.

drugs.name: Midazolam
drugs.indications: Deep sedation when propofol unsuitable; status epilepticus; alcohol withdrawal adjunct
drugs.adultDose: Bolus 1-2 mg (0.01-0.05 mg/kg) IV; infusion 0.02-0.1 mg/kg/h.
drugs.cautions: Associated with delirium and prolonged ventilation; avoid as routine sedative.

drugs.name: Haloperidol
drugs.indications: Distressing hyperactive delirium/agitation endangering safety (not routine)
drugs.adultDose: 2.5-5 mg IV every 6-8 h as needed (max ~20 mg/day; lower in elderly).
drugs.cautions: QTc prolongation (check ECG, avoid if QTc > 500 ms), extrapyramidal effects, NMS.

drugs.name: Quetiapine
drugs.adultDose: 25-50 mg orally/NG every 12 h, titrate to 200 mg twice daily.

drugs.name: Melatonin
drugs.adultDose: 3-10 mg orally/NG at night (doses in trials vary).

drugs.name: Cisatracurium (or atracurium)
drugs.indications: Severe ARDS, refractory raised ICP, shivering during TTM, ventilator dyssynchrony
drugs.adultDose: 0.15-0.2 mg/kg bolus, then 1-3 mcg/kg/min (ACURASYS fixed 37.5 mg/h); atracurium 0.5 mg/kg then 0.3-0.6 mg/kg/h.
drugs.cautions: Must ensure deep sedation and analgesia first; ICU-acquired weakness; eye care.

drugs.name: Diazepam
drugs.adultDose: 10-20 mg IV/oral every 1-2 h (symptom-triggered or front-loading) until CIWA-Ar < 10 or light sedation; IV boluses 5-10 mg every 5-10 min for severe withdrawal/DTs.
drugs.cautions: Accumulation in liver disease and elderly (use lorazepam); respiratory depression.

drugs.name: Lorazepam
drugs.indications: Alcohol withdrawal in liver failure or elderly
drugs.adultDose: 1-4 mg IV every 5-15 min for severe withdrawal, or 2-4 mg oral every 1-2 h symptom-triggered.
drugs.verify: IV lorazepam availability varies in India.

drugs.name: Phenobarbital
drugs.indications: Benzodiazepine-resistant alcohol withdrawal (or monotherapy protocols in ICU)
drugs.adultDose: 10 mg/kg IV over 30 min (single loading dose, ideal body weight), or 130-260 mg IV every 15-30 min titrated.
drugs.cautions: Respiratory depression with benzodiazepines; long half-life.

drugs.name: Thiamine
drugs.indications: Prevention/treatment of Wernicke encephalopathy in alcohol use or malnutrition
drugs.adultDose: Prevention 100-200 mg IV daily; suspected Wernicke 200-500 mg IV three times daily for 3-5 days; give before glucose.
drugs.verify: Dose for Wernicke varies between guidelines (200-500 mg TDS).
